questions.question: Which 5 countries have the most customers? Show the number of customers for each.
questions.agent_sql:
SELECT Country, COUNT(*) AS CustomerCount
FROM Customer
GROUP BY Country
ORDER BY CustomerCount DESC, Country ASC
LIMIT 5
questions.gold_sql: SELECT Country, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM Customer GROUP BY Country ORDER BY customers DESC LIMIT 5
questions.answer: The 5 countries with the most customers are the USA (13 customers), Canada (8 customers), Brazil (5 customers), France (5 customers), and Germany (4 customers).

questions.question: Which 5 genres have the most tracks? Show the track count for each.
questions.agent_sql:
SELECT g.Name AS Genre, COUNT(t.TrackId) AS TrackCount
FROM Genre g
JOIN Track t ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
GROUP BY g.Name
ORDER BY TrackCount DESC
LIMIT 5
questions.gold_sql: SELECT g.Name, COUNT(*) AS tracks FROM Track t JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId GROUP BY g.GenreId, g.Name ORDER BY tracks DESC LIMIT 5
questions.answer: The 5 genres with the most tracks are Rock (1,297 tracks), Latin (579 tracks), Metal (374 tracks), Alternative & Punk (332 tracks), and Jazz (130 tracks).

questions.question: Which 3 artists have released the most albums? Show the album count.
questions.agent_sql:
SELECT ar.Name AS ArtistName, COUNT(al.AlbumId) AS AlbumCount
FROM Artist ar
JOIN Album al ON ar.ArtistId = al.ArtistId
GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name
ORDER BY AlbumCount DESC, ArtistName ASC
LIMIT 3;
questions.gold_sql: SELECT ar.Name, COUNT(*) AS albums FROM Album al JOIN Artist ar ON ar.ArtistId = al.ArtistId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name ORDER BY albums DESC LIMIT 3
questions.answer: The 3 artists with the most albums are Iron Maiden with 21 albums, Led Zeppelin with 14 albums, and Deep Purple with 11 albums.

questions.question: What is the average track length in minutes for each genre, rounded to 2 decimals?
questions.agent_sql:
SELECT 
    g.Name AS GenreName,
    ROUND(AVG(t.Milliseconds) / 60000.0, 2) AS AvgMinutes
FROM Track t
JOIN Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
GROUP BY g.Name
ORDER BY AvgMinutes DESC;
questions.gold_sql: SELECT g.Name, ROUND(AVG(t.Milliseconds) / 60000, 2) AS avg_minutes FROM Track t JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId GROUP BY g.GenreId, g.Name
questions.answer: The average track length in minutes for each genre (calculated by dividing the track duration in milliseconds by 60,000) ranges from 2.24 minutes for Rock And Roll up to 48.53 minutes for Sci Fi & Fantasy.

questions.question: For each sales support agent, how many invoices did their customers generate and what was the total revenue?
questions.agent_sql:
SELECT 
    e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS AgentName,
    COUNT(i.InvoiceId) AS InvoiceCount,
    ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS TotalRevenue
FROM Employee e
JOIN Customer c ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId
JOIN Invoice i ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
WHERE e.Title = 'Sales Support Agent'
GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName, e.LastName
ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC;
questions.gold_sql: SELECT e.FirstName, e.LastName, COUNT(*) AS invoices, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS revenue FROM Employee e JOIN Customer c ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName, e.LastName
questions.answer: Jane Peacock's customers generated 146 invoices with a total revenue of $833.04. Margaret Park's customers generated 140 invoices totaling $775.40 in revenue, and Steve Johnson's customers generated 126 invoices totaling $720.16 in revenue.

questions.question: Which 3 artists have earned the most revenue from track sales?
questions.agent_sql:
SELECT 
    ar.Name AS ArtistName, 
    ROUND(SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity), 2) AS TotalRevenue
FROM Artist ar
JOIN Album al ON ar.ArtistId = al.ArtistId
JOIN Track t ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
JOIN InvoiceLine il ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name
ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC
LIMIT 3;
questions.gold_sql: SELECT ar.Name, ROUND(SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity), 2) AS revenue FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId JOIN Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId JOIN Artist ar ON ar.ArtistId = al.ArtistId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 3
questions.answer: The three artists who have earned the most revenue from track sales are Iron Maiden with $138.60, U2 with $105.93, and Metallica with $90.09.

questions.question: Show total revenue for each year together with the previous year's revenue.
questions.agent_sql:
WITH YearlyRevenue AS (
    SELECT 
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM InvoiceDate) AS InvoiceYear,
        ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS TotalRevenue
    FROM Invoice
    GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM InvoiceDate)
)
SELECT 
    InvoiceYear,
    TotalRevenue,
    LAG(TotalRevenue) OVER (ORDER BY InvoiceYear) AS PreviousYearRevenue
FROM YearlyRevenue
ORDER BY InvoiceYear;
questions.gold_sql: WITH y AS (SELECT YEAR(InvoiceDate) AS yr, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS revenue FROM Invoice GROUP BY yr) SELECT yr, revenue, LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY yr) AS prev_revenue FROM y ORDER BY yr
questions.answer: The total revenue for each year along with the previous year's revenue is as follows: in 2009, revenue was $449.46; in 2010, revenue rose to $481.45 (with a previous year revenue of $449.46); in 2011, revenue was $469.58 (previous year $481.45); in 2012, revenue was $477.53 (previous year $469.58); and in 2013, revenue was $450.58 (previous year $477.53).

questions.question: For the most recent year in the data, show revenue for each month and a running total.
questions.agent_sql:
WITH monthly_revenue AS (
  SELECT 
    strftime(InvoiceDate, '%Y-%m') AS month,
    ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS revenue
  FROM Invoice
  WHERE strftime(InvoiceDate, '%Y') = (
    SELECT strftime(MAX(InvoiceDate), '%Y') FROM Invoice
  )
  GROUP BY month
)
SELECT 
  month,
  revenue,
  ROUND(SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS running_total
FROM monthly_revenue
ORDER BY month;
questions.gold_sql: WITH m AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', InvoiceDate) AS month, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS revenue FROM Invoice WHERE YEAR(InvoiceDate) = (SELECT MAX(YEAR(InvoiceDate)) FROM Invoice) GROUP BY month) SELECT revenue, ROUND(SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS running_total FROM m ORDER BY month

questions.question: Which employee has the most direct reports, and how many?
questions.agent_sql:
SELECT 
    manager.FirstName || ' ' || manager.LastName AS ManagerName,
    manager.Title AS ManagerTitle,
    COUNT(employee.EmployeeId) AS DirectReportsCount
FROM Employee manager
JOIN Employee employee ON manager.EmployeeId = employee.ReportsTo
GROUP BY manager.EmployeeId, manager.FirstName, manager.LastName, manager.Title
ORDER BY DirectReportsCount DESC
LIMIT 1;
questions.gold_sql: SELECT m.FirstName, m.LastName, COUNT(*) AS direct_reports FROM Employee e JOIN Employee m ON m.EmployeeId = e.ReportsTo GROUP BY m.EmployeeId, m.FirstName, m.LastName ORDER BY direct_reports DESC LIMIT 1
questions.answer: Nancy Edwards, the Sales Manager, has the most direct reports with a total of 3 direct reports.

questions.question: How many customers spent more than the average customer?
questions.agent_sql:
WITH customer_totals AS (
    SELECT c.CustomerId, SUM(i.Total) AS total_spent
    FROM Customer c
    JOIN Invoice i ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
    GROUP BY c.CustomerId
),
avg_spent AS (
    SELECT AVG(total_spent) AS mean_spent FROM customer_totals
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_above_avg
FROM customer_totals, avg_spent
WHERE customer_totals.total_spent > avg_spent.mean_spent
questions.gold_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) AS spent FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM s WHERE spent > (SELECT AVG(spent) FROM s)
questions.answer: There are 22 customers who spent more than the average total amount spent per customer.
